title: Record the non-weight-3 masks missed by the c=7 witness.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Exhaustive finite census of one word. No new κ, and the selected frontier is unchanged.

On the length-42 floor word recorded in PR #7016,

```text
023514103524310254054123145203452034213150
```

every pair `0 ≤ s ≤ t ≤ 41` was evaluated. Of the 43 nonzero binary masks of weight other than 3, this word realizes 41. The missing masks are `(3, 5)` and `(0, 1, 3, 5)`. The same census misses the weight-3 mask `(1, 3, 5)`, which #7016 already records. That line is a control that this is the same word. It is not a new proof of the one-pair cover bound.

A depth-two block needs every nonzero mask, so this word is not a block. The census does not say that every six-source floor word at characteristic 7 misses these masks, and it does not decide whether a depth-two block exists. Masks that contain `{3, 5}` and are outside the three-mask missing list are realized, including `(0, 3, 5)` and `(1, 2, 3, 5)`. No supplier, consumer, or selected conditional κ changes. The selected record remains `781451/250000000` from PR #6030.

Evidence class: exhaustive finite census. The domain is the finite set of 903 pairs. The enumeration visits each pair, and the visit count is checked against `42*43/2`. A failed or incomplete search is not this claim, and the claim is not a proof of unrestricted nonexistence.

## Task and overlap

Base commit `17469fff78c22941280f04d39dc5a1faee09c840` (upstream `main`, re-fetched and unchanged). This fork's `main` is older, so the PR base is the pin branch `cursor/upstream-17469fff-pin-5ae9` at that same commit. The diff is only `research/six-source-c7-witness-other-weights/`.

Task card `connector-alphabet-change`, priority revision 8. Scope status: **changed**. The card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the alphabet fixed and answers open question 2 of PR #7016. A new operation is not the missing step.

Overlap checked 2026-11-10. GitHub search of upstream pull requests for the witness literal and for "non-weight-3" returns only open #7016, which poses the question and does not answer it. #7016 has no review comments. Local notes at the pinned main (complete inventory, 10178 README/TASK records) contain no earlier census of this word. The one-pair obstruction of #7016 is not repeated. The two-pair weight-3 question, open question 1 of PR #7016, is not taken.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only, from the repository root:

```sh
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/six-source-c7-witness-other-weights/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/six-source-c7-witness-other-weights/verify.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/six-source-c7-witness-other-weights --check-only
```

Both replay commands print:

`PASS_SIX_SOURCE_C7_WITNESS_OTHER_WEIGHTS pairs=903 nonzero_hit=60/63 other_hit=41/43 missing_other=(3,5);(0,1,3,5) weight3_missing=(1,3,5) zero_pairs=8 boundary42_new=0 superset_realized=13/16 controls=7`

The metadata check prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)`.

The seven controls are the floor-word shape, agreement of the allowed-set and mod-7 readings on every pair, the weight identity on every nonzero hit, three hand-checked prefixes (`(0, 1)`, `(0, 3)`, `(0, 6)`) together with the recorded weight-3 gap, the empty boundary-42 increment, the 13 realized masks among the 16 that contain `{3, 5}`, and two negative words: an adjacent transposition with a different non-weight-3 missing set, and a one-letter edit rejected for call count. Failures raise `SystemExit`. No SAT solver, Lean, Docker, other-word search, or selected-frontier replay was run.

## Credit

The depth-two interface and the weight identity are Nick Petalas's (PR #4231, PR #4248, PR #6107), with the Ross Richardson PR #934 / PR #943 lineage. JosieElliston's PR #6141 leaves characteristic 7 open. The diagonal equality case is upstream PR #6941. The witness and the question are open question 2 of upstream PR #7016 / fork PR 179.

Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can one explicit six-source length-42 floor word, other than this witness, realize both `(3, 5)` and `(0, 1, 3, 5)`? *Why:* a depth-two block needs both masks. This census shows that the recorded witness misses both. One other word that realizes both would separate that miss from the floor-word hypotheses. An exhaustive census of every floor word would be a different claim. *First step:* evaluate the same 903-pair predicate on one other concrete length-42 floor word and record, for these two masks only, whether each is realized. *Blocked by:* only the recorded witness is enumerated here, and no second characteristic-7 floor word is certified in this package. The two-pair weight-3 exchange remains open question 1 of PR #7016.
